scope: Primary-source research; benchmarks and numerical recommendations are independently derived from the stated model equations. This is not an exhaustive catalogue of decay channels.

sources.authors: Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; A. Takenaka et al.
sources.title: Search for proton decay via p→e+π0 and p→μ+π0 with an enlarged fiducial volume in Super-Kamiokande I-IV
sources.note: No e+π0 candidates; the μ+π0 candidate is consistent with expected atmospheric-neutrino background. No confirmed proton decay.

sources.authors: Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; K. Abe et al.
sources.title: Search for Proton Decay via p→νK+ using 260 kiloton·year data of Super-Kamiokande
sources.note: Channel bounds cannot be used as measured or universal total lifetimes.

sources.title: Search for proton decay via p→e+π0π0 and p→μ+π0π0 in 0.401 megaton-years exposure of Super-Kamiokande I-V
sources.status: primary collaboration paper; check journal metadata before labelling peer reviewed
sources.note: One candidate per channel, both consistent with background.

sources.authors: Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; Y. M. Liu et al.
sources.title: Search for proton decay into a single charged antilepton and a massless invisible particle using the full pure water data set of Super-Kamiokande
sources.status: preprint v1 available before research cutoff
sources.note: 401 kiloton-year exposure; no significant indication beyond background.

sources.authors: Borexino Collaboration; M. Agostini et al.
sources.title: A test of electric charge conservation with Borexino
sources.note: This hypothetical electron decay violates electric charge conservation. Bound is not evidence of instability. Stable electron is the standard-model choice.

sources.title: Particle creation by black holes
sources.note: Hawking temperature and thermal emission; ideal Stefan–Boltzmann lifetime used below is a simplified derived implementation, not an exact all-species evaporation calculation.

sources.title: Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole
sources.note: Greybody transmission and emitted species change luminosity and lifetime coefficients. Historical massless-neutrino assumptions must not be copied uncritically for modern stellar-mass holes.

sources.authors: Fred C. Adams and Gregory Laughlin
sources.title: A Dying Universe: The Long Term Fate and Evolution of Astrophysical Objects
sources.note: Gas-star formation decline around 10^12–10^13 yr, low-mass stars around 10^13 yr, conventional stellar era transition around 10^14–10^15 yr; dynamical stellar escape around 10^19–10^20 yr is model dependent. Degenerate/black-hole/dark-era transitions assume particle physics, especially proton decay. These are approximate ranges, not measured dates or mandatory boundaries.

sources.title: Black Dwarf Supernova in the Far Future
sources.note: Assuming no proton decay, black-dwarf collapse is estimated to start around 10^1100 yr for ~1.35 solar masses; ~10^1600 yr for ~1.24 solar masses; ~10^32000 yr at ~1.16 solar masses is especially uncertain at low density. Thus no such event within a 10^1000 yr endpoint. Not the fate of all remnants.

sources.authors: Anders Andreassen, William Frost, Matthew D. Schwartz
sources.title: Scale Invariant Instantons and the Complete Lifetime of the Standard Model
sources.note: Updated v4 reports 10^139 yr and >10^58 yr at 95% within its Standard Model calculation and inputs. This is not an observational prediction or universal universe expiry date; highly sensitive to top mass, strong coupling, matching, and physics beyond assumptions.

sources.authors: Gudrun Hiller, Tim Höhne, Daniel F. Litim, Tom Steudtner
sources.title: Vacuum Stability in the Standard Model and Beyond
sources.note: Stability centrally depends on top mass and strong coupling; decreasing uncertainties by factors ~2–3 could settle Standard Model stability at 5 sigma. New physics can alter stability. This work does not calculate a tunnelling lifetime; do not attribute one to it.

sources.authors: Robert R. Caldwell, Marc Kamionkowski, Nevin N. Weinberg
sources.title: Phantom Energy and Cosmic Doomsday
sources.note: Persistent phantom energy can produce scale-factor and density divergence in finite proper time. A possibility under assumptions, not established fate.

sources.authors: G. W. Gibbons and S. W. Hawking
sources.title: Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation
sources.note: Pure de Sitter horizon thermal response; T_dS=ħH/(2πkB). Do not replace redshifted CMB T0/a with this number; display CMB and horizon temperature separately.

sources.authors: CODATA; P. J. Mohr et al.
sources.title: CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2022
sources.note: c=299792458 m/s; G=6.67430e-11 SI; h=6.62607015e-34 J s; kB=1.380649e-23 J/K. h, c and kB are exact SI values; G has measurement uncertainty.

decay.equation: N(t)/N0 = exp[-(t-t0)/tau] for an explicitly assumed constant mean lifetime; half-life=tau*ln(2). Use comoving populations, or include a^-3 when reporting physical number density.
decay.defaults: Provide Stable explicitly; any finite lifetime is a user scenario. An experimental lower bound is not a selected lifetime or probability distribution.
decay.validation: At elapsed t=tau, fraction=exp(-1). At elapsed t=tau*ln(2), fraction=0.5. Stable fraction=1. To compare with a channel constraint L, use tau/B>L, not tau>L unless B=1.
decay.largeTimes: Keep u=log10(elapsed years), v=log10(tau years); log survival=-10^(u-v). Distinguish numerical underflow from physically exactly zero. Last decay in a finite population is stochastic and is not at t=tau.

hawking.remainingMassEquation: M(t)=M0*(1-t/tau)^(1/3), 0<=t<tau, with the endpoint identified as a semiclassical breakdown/event
hawking.validation: Doubling initial mass multiplies lifetime by 8 and halves initial temperature. At t=7*tau/8, remaining mass=M0/2. A 10^11 solar-mass hole has ideal lifetime ~2.10e100 yr; increasing the allowed mass range moves the nominal end of the black-hole era.
hawking.limitations: Isolated, neutral, nonrotating ideal blackbody approximation; greybody factors, particle species, accretion/background absorption, mergers, spin and quantum-gravity endpoint are omitted. Do not call exact. Net evaporation needs background sufficiently cool; distinguish CMB temperature from de Sitter horizon temperature.

vacuum.default: Unknown; no assumed decay event. Do not publish a measured vacuum-decay clock or assign model-fate probabilities.
vacuum.optionalScenario: An explicitly user-selected local Poisson hazard lambda per year can give S(t)=exp(-lambda*deltaT), but label this an illustrative effective model. A physical nucleation rate is per four-volume; observer survival is exp[-integral Gamma dV4] over the relevant past light cone, not an arbitrary universal global timer. The proper rate and ultraviolet physics are unknown.
vacuum.postEvent: Terminate this model branch at the event; do not animate a scientifically asserted post-decay universe.

recommendedModels.futureEras: Use approximate, conditional event windows. Never remove baryonic remnants at a fixed 10^37–10^40 yr if proton decay is disabled. Never mark black-dwarf supernova before 10^1100 yr in the cited model. Avoid modern factual claims from 1997 dark-matter candidate assumptions.
recommendedModels.extremeRange: Store u=log10(time/yr), so 10^1000 is u=1000. This alone is insufficient for de Sitter a: ln(a)~H*t itself exceeds a Number at large u. Store ln(a) in signed-log/layered form or return honest symbolic asymptotes. For de Sitter, log10(ln(a))~u+log10(H_per_year); a=exp(10^[u+log10(H_per_year)]). Similarly log densities and temperatures may require signed layered values. Do not clamp time to 10^308 or all values to zero/infinity and still claim physical coverage.
recommendedModels.integration: Integrate the FLRW system over its numerical interval with error-controlled steps; hand off to labelled matched asymptotes only once subdominant terms fall below a stated tolerance. Future CPL extrapolation w(a)=w0+wa(1-a) is phenomenological and unbounded; its exp[3wa(a-1)] factor requires log-safe evaluation and an explicit extrapolation warning. Branches with a finite rip or crunch stop at that event, rather than continuing to 10^1000.

analyticBenchmarks.name: Einstein-de Sitter
analyticBenchmarks.checks: t0=2/(3H0); expansion increasing, density*a^3 constant, Tcmb*a constant

analyticBenchmarks.name: Pure de Sitter
analyticBenchmarks.solution: a=exp(H0*deltaT), H=H0, q=-1, event-horizon proper radius=c/H0; future lifetime infinite

analyticBenchmarks.name: Flat constant-w fluid
analyticBenchmarks.phantomExample: w=-1.5: H0*(tRip-t0)=4/3; at deltaT=(tRip-t0)/2, a=2^(4/3), H=2H0. Big Rip remaining-time formula including sqrt(OmegaDE) is only a dark-energy-dominated approximation in mixed matter models.
analyticBenchmarks.stopRule: Do not take a fractional power after its bracket changes sign or continue beyond tRip.

analyticBenchmarks.name: Closed dust recollapse
analyticBenchmarks.solution: A=Omega_m/[2*(Omega_m-1)], B=Omega_m/[2*H0*(Omega_m-1)^(3/2)]; a=A*(1-cos eta), t=B*(eta-sin eta), eta in [0,2pi]. aMax=Omega_m/(Omega_m-1), tTurn=pi*B, tCrunch=2pi*B. eta0=acos(2/Omega_m-1) on expanding branch.
analyticBenchmarks.numericCase: Omega_m=2, Omega_k=-1: aMax=2; H0*t0=pi/2-1; H0*(tTurn-t0)=pi/2+1; H0*(tCrunch-t0)=3pi/2+1.
analyticBenchmarks.checks: H crosses from positive to negative at the finite aMax. Solving only H=+sqrt(F) cannot recollapse. A log(a) independent variable also fails at the turn unless branch handling is explicit. Locate F(a)=0; never clamp negative F to a frozen universe.

analyticBenchmarks.name: Dust plus negative cosmological constant
analyticBenchmarks.solution: a=(Omega_m/L)^(1/3)*sin(theta)^(2/3), theta=(3/2)H0*sqrt(L)*t; theta in (0,pi). aMax=(Omega_m/L)^(1/3); tCrunch=2pi/[3H0*sqrt(L)]. At a=1 on expansion, theta0=asin(sqrt(L/Omega_m)).
analyticBenchmarks.checks: Turn at theta=pi/2; shows positive spatial curvature is not necessary for recollapse with negative Lambda.

analyticBenchmarks.name: Friedmann and normalization residuals
analyticBenchmarks.solution: At a=1, E^2(1)=Omega_r+Omega_m+Omega_k+Omega_de=1. For computed background, test (H/H0)^2-E^2(a) within tolerance and model conservation scalings.
analyticBenchmarks.checks: Censor sample counts beyond terminal singularities; report numerical errors separately from observational uncertainties or model uncertainty.
